verdict.rationale: Obsidian's own architecture keeps data out of the vendor's reach. Notes are plain-text Markdown stored locally, giving the user 'total control over your data'. Sync is end-to-end encrypted by default, which the docs say 'guarantees that no one — not even the Obsidian team — can access your notes', so Obsidian structurally cannot train on that content. However, nothing in the evidence explicitly addresses AI model training. missing for 10: an explicit first-party no-AI-training policy or opt-out, coverage of Publish-hosted content (publicly hosted at publish.obsidian.md), independent corroboration of the no-training posture.
